title: Hold it instead of becoming it

blocks.promptMd: Which sentence describes a station and a log correctly?

choices.md: Either one — they mean the same thing in Python

blocks.explainMd: A station uses a log for one job among many; it is not a kind of log and could not stand in for one. Encoding that as an attribute keeps the log swappable and keeps the station’s public surface down to the methods a station should offer.

blocks.promptMd: Subclassing puts every public method of the base onto your class, whether or not those methods make sense there.
blocks.explainMd: That is the whole point of inheritance — the subclass can stand in for the base — but it means you inherit the base’s future as well as its present. Composition exposes only what you choose to forward, so a change inside the collaborator cannot widen your own interface.

blocks.promptMd: > `Station` currently inherits from `Log`. Rewrite it to **hold** a `Log` in `self.log` instead, keeping `record(line)` returning the number of lines so far. Output should be `1`.

hintLadder.md: Ask the is-a question about the starter: is a station a kind of log? Everything the log can do is currently on the station.
Drop the base class from the header, build a `Log()` in `Station.__init__`, and reach the log through that attribute.
Forward only what you mean to offer: `record` calls `self.log.add(line)`, and callers never learn that a `Log` is in there.

description: Hold a helper instead of inheriting from it.
